findings.reason: the node's own acceptance check must be narrowed to `cat-file --batch` or it never reads as "one function", and the inventory must either consolidate the neighbouring `git()` wrapper or state why it stays.
findings.text: the section claims to enumerate what is duplicated across the two files it edits, but the byte-identical `git()` wrapper (`reckon/interface_counts.py:54` and `reckon/velocity.py:145`) is a second, un-cited duplication; and the done-when's `grep -rn 'cat-file' reckon/` cannot isolate the batch reader because it also matches frozenset verb literals (`reckon/worker_git_shim.py:100`, `reckon/ledger.py:2298` and `:2310`), docstrings (`reckon/velocity.py:362`, `reckon/interface_counts.py:444`) and single-object `cat-file -e` checks (`reckon/crew/routing.py:1222`, `reckon/crew/promotion.py:3997`)

findings.reason: the node must pin the extracted interface to a spec-list batch reader (single-revision callers mapping `(revision, path)` pairs) or state that `_plan_metas` keeps its own loop, before it runs.
findings.text: the extracted public reader is described as returning "path to bytes for a revision", which fits the counter's single-revision call but not `_plan_metas`, whose specs span many commits and whose docstring says one `cat-file --batch` process serves every plan so a full-history census avoids "one subprocess per commit"; a per-revision interface forces `_plan_metas` back to a subprocess per commit or a second interface

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the one promoted reader is specified as returning bytes "for a revision", yet its second caller `velocity._plan_metas` batches an ordered list of `(sha, path)` specs across many commits in a single pass.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §10 folds a duplicate into its existing owner (velocity.py holds the loop and the cache root) rather than forking a parallel path, which is what this item asks for.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §10 states in its own text that public_definitions grows by exactly two and why nothing public can be retired.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §10 cites the mechanisms it searched (`interface_counts._read_blobs`, `velocity._plan_metas`, `_velocity_cache_root`, the clones tokenisation pair, the frozen census), but its inventory of what is duplicated in the two files it touches is incomplete and the search instrument it names is non-discriminating.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the change promotes the existing `cat-file --batch` loop to a public name rather than layering a new wrapper over an existing reader.
